Afterlife is a speculation concerning existence after death, in which the essential part of an individual's stream of consciousness or identity continues to exist after the death of their physical body.
As the first civilian director of central intelligence, he oversaw covert coups in Iran and Guatemala and the mind-control program MKUltra before Kennedy forced him out — who is he?
Allen Dulles (April 7, 1893 - January 29, 1969) was an American lawyer who was the first civilian director of central intelligence (DCI), and its longest serving director.
Before becoming the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations in 2017, this Portuguese Socialist led his country as prime minister from 1995 to 2002 — who is he?
António Guterres (born 30 April 1949) is a Portuguese and East Timorese politician and diplomat who, since 2017, has served as the ninth Secretary-General of the United Nations.

The unexpected victory of vastly outnumbered English troops over the French on 25 October 1415 during the Hundred Years' War boosted English morale and lasted until 1429. What historic battle was this?
Battle of Agincourt ((t)) was an English victory in the Hundred Years' War. The Battle of Agincourt ( AJ-in-kor(t); French: Azincourt [azɛ̃kuʁ]) was an English victory in the Hundred Years' War.
Recording six visions seen by a prophet exiled in Babylon between 593 and 571 BC, this prophetic text follows Isaiah and Jeremiah in the Christian Bible — which text?
Book of Ezekiel is the third of the Latter Prophets in the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible) and one of the major prophetic books in the Christian Bible, where it follows Isaiah and Jeremiah.

Charles G. Dawes (August 27, 1865 - April 23, 1951) was the 30th vice president of the United States from 1925 to 1929 under President Calvin Coolidge.
When a 1952 coup destroyed Cuba's emerging democracy, a young lawyer named Fidel Castro tried first through the courts—then took up arms. Which revolution overthrew Fulgencio Batista's dictatorship?
Cuban Revolution was the military and political movement that overthrew the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, who had ruled Cuba from 1952 to 1959.

Dmitry Utkin (11 June 1970 - 23 August 2023) was a Russian military officer and mercenary.

Erich Honecker (25 August 1912 - 29 May 1994) was a German communist politician who led the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) from 1971 until shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989.
Elected to the Académie Française in 1811, which French aristocrat defended the Catholic faith in his book 'The Genius of Christianity'?

This Virginia governor supported COVID-19 vaccination efforts while opposing mandates, and banned mask mandates in the state's public schools during his first year in office — who is he?
Glenn Youngkin (born December 9, 1966) is an American politician and businessman who served as the 74th governor of Virginia from 2022 to 2026.
An English general-practice doctor convicted in 2000 of murdering 15 of his own patients, he is reckoned one of history's most prolific killers with an estimated 250 victims. Who was he?
Harold Shipman (14 January 1946 - 13 January 2004) was an English doctor in general practice and serial killer.
Formed in 1942 from earlier Polish resistance cells, this underground force became one of WWII Europe's largest, fighting German occupiers under London-exiled leadership — which organization?
Home Army (abbreviated AK) was the dominant resistance movement in German-occupied Poland during World War II.
Nicknamed "Bougie," this former Knesset member and welfare minister followed his father into Israel's presidency in 2021 — who is he?
Isaac Herzog (born 22 September 1960) is an Israeli politician who has been serving since 2021 as the president of Israel.
The second son of one president and younger brother of another, this Republican politician served as Florida's governor from 1999 to 2007 before an unsuccessful 2016 presidential bid. Who is he?
Jeb Bush (born February 11, 1953) is an American politician and businessman who served as the 43rd governor of Florida from 1999 to 2007.
After ascending to Judah's throne at age eight, this king ordered major religious reforms once a long-lost scroll of the Law turned up during temple repairs — who is he?
Josiah or Yoshiyahu (Biblical Hebrew) was the 16th king of Judah (c. 640-609 BC).
Backed early on by the Viet Cong and Chinese Communists, this force grew in the forests of eastern Cambodia and later ruled the country as Democratic Kampuchea — which movement was it?
Khmer Rouge is the name that was popularly given to members of the Communist Party of Kampuchea (CPK), and by extension to Democratic Kampuchea, which ruled Cambodia between 1975 and 1979.
He joined the Communist youth league in 1923 and rose to run the Soviet Union for eighteen years, longer than anyone but Stalin — which leader?
Leonid Brezhnev (19 December 1906 - 10 November 1982) was a Soviet politician who served as General Secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from 1964 until his death in 1982.

This Indian politician and former investment banker, known for fiery speeches in Parliament, was expelled from the Lok Sabha in 2023 after being elected from Krishnanagar, only to win re-election in 2024 — who is she?
Mahua Moitra (Bengali; born 12 October 1974) is an Indian politician and former investment banker.
Dubbed the 'Father of the Steam Navy' for modernizing the fleet, this officer commanded ships in the War of 1812 before ending Japan's isolation — who was he?
Matthew C. Perry (April 10, 1794 - March 4, 1858) was a United States Navy officer who commanded ships in several wars, including the War of 1812 and the Mexican-American War.

After her three-time-president husband died in exile, this Panamanian widow took over both his coffee business and his political party — then in 1999 became the only woman ever to be elected president of Panama. Who is she?
Mireya Moscoso (born 1 July 1946) is a Panamanian politician who served as the President of Panama from 1999 to 2004.

Named crown prince in 2006 during his half-brother's reign, he finally ruled for just three years from 2020 until his death in 2023, grappling with internal political disputes. Which Kuwaiti leader is this?
Nawaf Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah (25 June 1937 - 16 December 2023) was Emir of Kuwait from 2020 until his death in 2023.
Born in British Hong Kong, this Canadian politician became a Toronto school board trustee in 1985, later served as an NDP member of Parliament, and has been mayor of Toronto since 2023 — who is she?
Olivia Chow (born March 24, 1957) is a Canadian politician who has been the 66th and current mayor of Toronto since 2023.
This Pakistani military officer overthrew Nawaz Sharif's government in a 1999 coup and went on to serve as the country's tenth president — who is he?
Pervez Musharraf (11 August 1943 - 5 February 2023) was a Pakistani politician and military officer who served as the tenth president of Pakistan from 2001 to 2008.

This Pennsylvania state treasurer, convicted of accepting a bribe in a state tax-processing scandal, shocked the nation by taking his own life live on camera during a 1987 press conference — who was he?
R. Budd Dwyer (November 21, 1939 - January 22, 1987) was an American politician who served as the 70th treasurer of Pennsylvania from 1981 until his suicide in 1987.
A right-wing populist with a reputation as abrasive and aggressive, this former cost accountant served as New Zealand's prime minister from 1975 to 1984. Who was he?
Robert Muldoon (25 September 1921 - 5 August 1992) was a New Zealand politician who served as the 31st prime minister of New Zealand, from 1975 to 1984, while leader of the National Party.
Said to fly through the night sky on Christmas Eve pulled by reindeer, this legendary gift-giver traces back to a 4th-century Greek bishop known for secret generosity — who is he?
Santa Claus is a legendary figure originating in Western Christian culture who is said to bring gifts during the late evening and overnight hours on Christmas Eve.
This Indian actress won acclaim for playing Tulsi Virani in a hit soap opera before pivoting to politics as a Bharatiya Janata Party leader who has held several Union Cabinet posts — who is she?

This American politician has served as junior U.S. senator from Texas since 2013, after earlier serving as the state's solicitor general and later chairing the Senate Commerce Committee — who is he?
Ted Cruz (born December 22, 1970) is an American politician and attorney serving as the junior United States senator from Texas since 2013.

Centered on the Armenian highlands between Lakes Van, Urmia, and Sevan, this Iron Age kingdom's territory stretched across modern Turkey, Iran, Iraq, Armenia, Georgia, and Azerbaijan — name the kingdom?

Urartu was an Iron Age kingdom centered on the Armenian highlands between Lake Van, Lake Urmia, and Lake Sevan. Its kings left behind cuneiform inscriptions in the Urartian language, a member of the Hurro-Urartian language family.

Wars of the Three Kingdoms is the collective term for a series of conflicts fought between 1639 and 1653 in England, Scotland and Ireland, then separate entities in a personal union under Charles I.

Boshin War: 1868–1869 Japanese civil war. When the Boshin War began, Japan was already modernizing, following the same course of advancement as that of the industrialized Western nations.
Cursed by Apollo to speak true prophecies that no one would ever believe, this Trojan priestess survived the fall of Troy only to be murdered alongside Agamemnon. Who was she?

House of Hohenzollern: German royal and imperial dynasty.

One of three major ancient Paleo-Balkan peoples alongside the Thracians and Greeks, this Indo-European group gave their name to a western Balkan region first described by a 6th-century-BC Greek writer — who were they?

John Franklin: British naval officer and explorer (1786–1847)

Konrad Adenauer: Chancellor of West Germany from 1949 to 1963. Adenauer belied his age by his intense work habits and his uncanny political instinct.
Born to a working-class family in Kamenskoye, he led the USSR as General Secretary from 1964 until his death — a tenure second in length only to Stalin's. Who was he?
Leonid Brezhnev: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1964 to 1982.
Nicknamed 'the Prudent,' this King of France defied his father in a 1440 revolt, married the Duke of Savoy's daughter against his father's wishes, and took the throne in 1461 — who is he?
Louis XI: King of France from 1461 to 1483.
Founded around 1400 by a ruler also known as Iskandar Shah, this Malay kingdom's port city became a major transshipment hub and center of Islamic learning -- which realm?
Malacca Sultanate: State on the Malay Peninsula, 1400–1511.
Commissioned as an armor officer after Princeton ROTC, this retired general served as Army chief of staff before President Trump named him the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff — who is he?

Oedipus: Mythical Greek king of Thebes. Oedipus (UK:, also US:; Ancient Greek: Οἰδίπους Oidípous, lit. 'swollen foot') was a mythical Greek king of Thebes.

Papal States: Italian state ruled by the pope (756–1870)
A close ally of Robespierre, this French revolutionary chose suicide over arrest when authorities stormed the Hôtel de Ville during the coup of 9–10 Thermidor — who was he?

An Abrahamic faith born in 1930s Jamaica, it has no central authority and centers on Jah — with many followers regarding Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia as the Second Coming. What is it?

This Elizabethan explorer and statesman helped defend England against the Spanish Armada while also playing a leading role in colonizing North America — who was he?

Which of these four dates back furthest?
Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Toghon Temür is an astronomer. Toghon Temür acceded to the throne in 1333 after years of succession disputes following his father's death.
Who among these is a mathematician?
John Horton Conway is a mathematician. John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 – 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
What is the atomic number of Caesium?
Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
What is the atomic number of Tungsten?
Tungsten (also called wolfram) is a chemical element; it has symbol W (from German: Wolfram) and atomic number 74.
In what year did Hamish Harding die?
Hamish Harding: George Hamish Livingston Harding (24 June 1964 – 18 June 2023) was a British businessman, pilot and adventurer based in the United Arab Emirates (UAE).
In what year was Pluto discovered?
Pluto (minor-planet number 134340) is a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, a ring of bodies beyond the orbit of Neptune.
TypeScript: Anders Hejlsberg. TypeScript (TS) is a high-level programming language that adds static typing with optional type annotations to JavaScript.
Pethidine: Pfizer. Pethidine, also known as meperidine and sold under the brand name Demerol among others, is a fully synthetic opioid pain medication of the phenylpiperidine class.
Who is credited with discovering Archaeopteryx?
Archaeopteryx: Carl Friedrich Häberlein. Archaeopteryx (lit. 'ancient wing'), sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is an extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Who is credited with discovering Oganesson?
Oganesson: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Who is credited with discovering Cimetidine?
Cimetidine: John Colin Emmett. Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Who is credited with discovering Iridium?
Iridium: Smithson Tennant. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
A broad-spectrum benzimidazole drug, this medicine clears intestinal parasites from pinworm to hookworm to tapeworm — which agent is it?
Albendazole is a broad-spectrum antihelmintic and antiprotozoal agent of the benzimidazole type.
A balloon-like bulge at a weakened patch of vessel wall, it can turn lethal in the brain's circle of Willis or the aorta if it bursts — what is this?
Aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall.
Founder of a prominent Russian design studio and an avid, famously foul-mouthed blogger, this designer and entrepreneur is also a member of the Tolstoy family — name this designer?
Artemy Lebedev (born 13 February 1975) is a Russian designer, entrepreneur and Internet personality.
Built under license from the Swiss Pilatus PC-9, this turboprop trainer serves the US Air Force, Navy, and Marine Corps and flies in Canada under the designation CT-156 Harvard — which aircraft?
Beechcraft T-6 Texan II is a single-engined, turboprop aircraft currently built by Textron Aviation, formerly manufactured by Raytheon Aircraft Company, which sold to Textron in 2007.
Born as Hughes Helicopters' Model 77 to replace the AH-1 Cobra, this twin-turboshaft attack helicopter packs a 30 mm chain gun and Hellfire missiles in a tandem cockpit — what is it?
Boeing AH-64 Apache (-) is an American twin-turboshaft attack helicopter with a tailwheel-type landing gear and a tandem cockpit for a crew of two.

Synthesized by the liver in response to inflammation, this ring-shaped blood molecule binds to the surface of dead or dying cells to activate the immune system's complement cascade. What is it commonly called?
C-reactive protein (CRP) is an annular (ring-shaped) pentameric protein found in blood plasma, whose circulating concentration rises in response to inflammation.
Which metabolic process is the polar opposite of anabolism, breaking large molecules such as proteins and lipids down into monomers while releasing energy, some of it lost as heat?
Catabolism is the set of metabolic pathways that breaks down molecules into smaller units that are either oxidized to release energy or used in other anabolic reactions.
Linked to repeated head trauma, this worsening neurodegenerative disease turns up in boxers and footballers — and even in soccer players, largely from heading the ball. What is it?

Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a neurodegenerative disease linked to repeated trauma to the head. The encephalopathy symptoms can include behavioral problems, mood problems, and problems with thinking.
This highly poisonous member of the carrot family can grow to nearly 8 feet tall, with hollow, maroon-spotted stems and a famously unpleasant odor — what plant is it?
Conium maculatum (British English) or poison hemlock (in North America), is a highly poisonous flowering plant and a nitrophile weed species in the carrot family Apiaceae.
Nearly every genus in this taxonomic family of armadillos is extinct, except for one genus that still includes eight living species today. Name the family?
Dasypodidae is a family of mostly extinct genera of armadillos.
What flying insect, of which about 3,000 species exist, is known for its large compound eyes, two pairs of transparent wings, and often iridescent, metallic body coloration?
Dragonfly is a flying insect belonging to the infraorder Anisoptera below the order Odonata.
This discipline systematically applies natural science and mathematics to design solutions like bridges, pacemakers, and spacecraft under real-world constraints. What field is it?
Engineering is the practice of systematically applying natural science and mathematics to design and improve systems, devices, or processes that solve problems under constraints.
Colloquially called 'squirting,' this phenomenon involves fluid from the Skene's gland and is physiologically distinct from coital incontinence — what is it?
Female ejaculation is characterized as an expulsion of fluid from the Skene's gland at the lower end of the urethra during or before an orgasm.
This American video game businessman dropped out of Harvard to join Microsoft, where he worked on early Windows and a Doom port, before co-founding Valve Corporation in 1996 — who is he?
Gabe Newell (born November 3, 1962), also known by his nickname GabeN, is an American video game developer and businessman.
Comprising about 50 species native to tropical regions worldwide, this genus produces roughly 80% of the world's natural fiber and doubles as an oilseed crop — which genus?
Gossypium is a genus of flowering plants in the tribe Gossypieae of the mallow family, Malvaceae, from which cotton is harvested.

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.
This Confederate veteran and pharmacist sold the rights to his 1886 beverage recipe to Asa Griggs Candler for about $2,300 shortly before he died — who is he?
John Stith Pemberton (July 8, 1831 - August 16, 1888) was an American pharmacist, chemist, and Confederate States Army officer who is best known as the inventor of Coca-Cola.
Originally a water-retrieving gun dog from Italy's Po Delta marshes, this breed later became prized for hunting truffles once its wetland habitat was drained — what breed is it?
Lagotto Romagnolo is an Italian breed of dog.
Named after a pioneer of sterile surgery, this genus of rod-shaped bacteria can multiply even at refrigerator temperatures and causes a rare but serious foodborne illness — what is it?
Listeria is a genus of bacteria that acts as an intracellular parasite in mammals.
Formed from two glucose units linked by an alpha(1→4) bond, which disaccharide, a reducing sugar unlike sucrose, is released when starch breaks down during malting?
Maltose (or), also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an (14) bond.
More than 80% of cases trace to asbestos exposure, and it grows from the thin lining covering the lungs and other organs — which cancer is it?
Mesothelioma is a type of cancer that develops from the thin layer of tissue that covers many of the internal organs (known as the mesothelium).
This genus of edible sac fungi has a honeycomb-like cap of ridges and pits, is prized in French and Catalan cooking, and turns toxic if eaten raw or undercooked. What fungus is this?
Morchella is a genus of edible sac fungi closely related to anatomically simpler cup fungi in the order Pezizales (division Ascomycota).

Encompassing three distinct genetic conditions marked by nervous-system tumors, one type brings café au lait skin spots and scoliosis while another causes early-onset hearing loss and cataracts — which condition?
Neurofibromatosis (NF) refers to a group of three distinct genetic conditions in which tumors grow in the nervous system.
Which applied-math discipline, born from pre-WWII military planning and overlapping heavily with industrial engineering, hunts for the maximum profit or minimum cost in real-world problems?

Operations research (British), often shortened to the initialism OR, is a branch of applied mathematics that deals with the development and application of analytical methods to improve management and decision-making.
This Scottish biologist-turned-town-planner coined the word 'conurbation' and his work contains one of the earliest versions of 'think globally, act locally.' Who was he?
Patrick Geddes (2 October 1854 - 17 April 1932) was a Scottish biologist, sociologist, Comtean positivist, geographer, philanthropist and pioneering town planner.
This genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae is found mainly in northern South America, with a single species ranging into Central America — name this genus?
Phoneutria is a genus of spiders in the family Ctenidae.

Native to most of the Northern Hemisphere, this genus of 25 to 30 deciduous tree species includes poplars, aspens, and cottonwoods, one of which was the first tree ever fully DNA-sequenced — which genus?
Populus is a genus of 25-30 species of deciduous flowering plants in the family Salicaceae, native to most of the Northern Hemisphere.
This yellow-white fluid forms at sites of infection and inflammation — when trapped in tissue it's called an abscess, and near the skin's surface a pimple — name the substance?
Pus is an exudate, typically white-yellow, yellow, or yellow-brown, formed at the site of inflammation during infections, regardless of cause.
Also known as vitamin B2, this nutrient builds two key coenzymes for energy metabolism and may, taken orally, cut down on migraine headaches in adults — what is it?
Riboflavin is a vitamin found in food and sold as a dietary supplement.
Having coded his first game in high school and studied computer science in Tokyo, this man went on to lead Nintendo by championing fun over raw horsepower — who is he?
Satoru Iwata (December 6, 1959 - July 11, 2015) was a Japanese businessman, video game programmer and producer.
Element number 14 is a tetravalent non-metal sometimes called a metalloid, prized for the transistors and integrated circuits it makes possible — which one is it?
Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
A self-taught Indian genius of infinite series and number theory, he initially struggled to interest established mathematicians because his methods were so unfamiliar — who was he?
Srinivasa Ramanujan (22 December 1887 - 26 April 1920) was an Indian mathematician who worked during the early 20th century.
Deriving its name from a French word for crushed oak bark used in hide-curing, this class of astringent plant compounds binds to and precipitates proteins and other organic molecules — what is it?
Tannin (or tannoids) are a class of astringent, polyphenolic biomolecules that bind to and precipitate proteins and various other organic compounds including amino acids and alkaloids.
This genus of about 30 tree and shrub species is native across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, with its greatest diversity found in Asia — what genus is it?
Tilia is a genus of about 30 species of trees or bushes, native throughout most of the temperate Northern Hemisphere.
What is the medical term for having dangerously high levels of urea in the blood, typically caused by kidney failure?

Uremia is the condition of having high levels of urea in the blood. It is the signs, symptoms and results from laboratory tests which result from inadequate excretory, regulatory, and endocrine function of the kidneys.
These big cetaceans — everything in the group except dolphins and porpoises — count the hippopotamus as their closest living relative on land. What are they?
Whale are a widely distributed and diverse group of fully aquatic placental marine mammals.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Though commonly called a nut, this tree's fruit is technically a drupe with a hard shell surrounding an edible seed, closely related to the peach — which food is it?
Almond: Species of nut. The fruit of the almond is a drupe, consisting of an outer hull and a hard shell with the seed, which is not a true nut.
Despite helping develop the Soviet Union's thermonuclear weapons, this physicist won the 1975 Nobel Peace Prize for his human-rights activism and was later persecuted as a dissident — who was he?
Andrei Sakharov: Soviet nuclear physicist and human rights activist (1921–1989)
The average adult sheds 50 to 70 billion cells a day through this tidy, programmed cell death — named from a Greek word for 'falling off' — quite unlike messy, traumatic necrosis. What is it?
Apoptosis: Form of programmed cell death. Because apoptosis cannot stop once it has begun, it is a highly regulated process.
Driven by elevated LDL cholesterol, this chronic inflammatory disease builds plaque lesions inside artery walls and can lead to stroke or coronary trouble — what is it?
Atherosclerosis: Inflammatory disease involving a buildup of lesions in the walls of arteries.

Developed in the 18th century by an English clergyman and, independently, by Pierre-Simon Laplace, this rule lets you flip a conditional probability — say, finding the odds a patient is sick given a positive test. What is it?
Bayes' theorem: Mathematical rule for inverting probabilities.
Colloquially called a buffalo in the US and Canada, this large bovine is actually more closely related to yaks and cattle than to true buffalo — which animal?
Hailing from the Anglo-Scottish frontier and frequently cited as the most intelligent dog breed on Earth, which sheepdog dominates sheepdog trials?
Border Collie: Working dog breed. The Border Collie is a breed of British herding dog of the collie type of medium size.
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Native to the Americas, this plant genus in the nightshade family produces the fruits we call peppers, including sweet bell types and fiery chilies — what genus is it?
This bacterial skin infection affects the dermis and subcutaneous fat, most often striking the legs or face and causing spreading redness and swelling — what is it?
Cellulitis: Bacterial infection of the inner layers of the skin called the dermis.
Known for a bitter metallic aftertaste that gets worse if you rinse with water, this antiseptic is used before surgery and to prevent dental plaque — what is it?
Chlorhexidine: Disinfectant and antiseptic. Chlorhexidine is a disinfectant and antiseptic which is used for skin disinfection before surgery and to disinfect surgical instruments.
This process turns blood from liquid to gel through platelet activation and fibrin formation, beginning almost instantly after a vessel is injured — what's the clotting process called?
Coagulation: Process of formation of blood clots. Coagulation, also known as clotting, is the process by which blood changes from a liquid to a gel forming a blood clot.

This physical law holds that within an isolated system, nothing is created or destroyed — only transformed, as when a stick of dynamite converts stored chemical potential into heat, sound, and motion — what law is it?
Conservation of energy: Law of physics and chemistry.
Squash, pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, and the plant behind loofah sponges all belong to which family, nicknamed the gourds?
Cucurbitaceae: Family of plants. The Cucurbitaceae ( kew-KUR-bih-TAY-see-ee), also called cucurbits or the gourd family, are a plant family consisting of about 965 species in 101 genera.
Often tied to diseases like Alzheimer's, this incurable, progressive syndrome erodes memory, language, and motivation in stages — which condition is being described?
Sold under the brand name Motilium, this dopamine-blocking medication treats nausea and slow stomach emptying, but also raises prolactin levels — what is it?
Credited as the first to create a transuranium element — neptunium — this Berkeley physicist shared the 1951 Nobel in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Also called Human Factors Engineering, this discipline applies psychology and physiology to reduce errors and boost safety in system design — what field?
Ergonomics: Designing systems to suit their users.
One of only two living species in its genus, this rodent was such a prized delicacy to the ancient Romans that its common name literally advertises the fact. What animal is it?
European edible dormouse: Species of rodent.
Known as the weeping fig and the official tree of Bangkok, this flowering plant native to Asia and Australia is often used as a biomonitor in cities — which species?
Ficus benjamina: Species of fig. The species is also naturalized in the West Indies and in the states of Florida and Arizona in the United States.
Working in Feynman's group on the Manhattan Project before co-detecting an elusive elementary particle with Clyde Cowan, he won the 1995 Nobel for catching the neutrino — who was he?
This field studies how geography shapes international relations and foreign policy, though critics have dismissed its early theories as pseudoscience — which discipline?
Geopolitics: Study of geography's effects on politics.
This Intel co-founder proposed the famous observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every two years — who is he?
This inherited disorder leaves blood unable to clot properly, causing prolonged bleeding after injury and, in its two main forms, low levels of clotting factor VIII or IX — which condition?
Haemophilia: Genetic disease involving blood clotting.

Governed by rules laid out in a document called a blazon, this medieval discipline of coats of arms, crests, and mottoes may have arisen so knights could recognize commanders behind their helmets — what is it?
Heraldry: Discipline of the design and study of coats of arms.
Running from your shoulder to your elbow, this long arm bone has a constriction nicknamed the 'surgical neck' due to its tendency to fracture — which bone?
Humerus: Long bone of the upper arm. It connects the scapula and the two bones of the lower arm, the radius and ulna, and consists of three sections.
Named from an Ancient Greek word for 'intestinal obstruction,' this medical condition disrupts the gut's normal propulsive movement, whether from lost peristalsis or a physical blockage — what is it?
Ileus: Disruption to the propulsive ability of the intestine.
A self-taught rocketeer and practicing occultist, this co-founder of both JPL and Aerojet invented the first castable composite rocket propellant before dying young in 1952. Who was he?
This English mathematician dreamed up the cellular automaton known as the Game of Life and spent his later years at Princeton — who was he?
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.

This catch-all name covers over 7,000 squamate species on every continent but Antarctica — from finger-length geckos to the three-meter Komodo dragon, with a few 'legless' lineages thrown in. What is it?
Found from Gibraltar to across Asia, these Old World monkeys live in troops centered on dominant matriarchs, and one Malaysian species eats about 70 rats a year — what are they?
Macaque: Genus of Old World monkeys. The macaques constitute a genus (Macaca) of gregarious Old World monkeys of the subfamily Cercopithecinae.
Prized by fur trappers for its yellowish-to-dark-brown coat, this bushy-tailed, weasel-like mammal is adapted to life in the taiga's coniferous forests — what is it?

Diagnosed when a person has at least three of five red flags -- including abdominal obesity and high blood pressure -- this cluster of conditions raises the risk of heart disease and diabetes in about a quarter of US adults. What is it?
Metabolic syndrome: Cluster of diseases occurring with obesity.

Prized for their fur and related to weasels and otters, these semiaquatic carnivores have established wild populations in Britain and Denmark after farm escapes and animal-rights releases — what are they?
Mink: Mammal in the family Mustelidae.
This contagious, vaccine-preventable viral disease is best known for causing painful swelling of the glands beside the jaw — its hallmark symptom. What is it?
Mumps: Human disease caused by paramyxovirus.
Discovered in 1885 by Carl Auer von Welsbach, this rare-earth element tarnishes quickly in air and produces pink, purple, and yellow compounds when oxidized — which element, atomic number 60?
Neodymium: Chemical element with atomic number 60 (Nd)

Sometimes called "radiology done inside out," this medical specialty records radiation emitted from within the body and emphasizes function over anatomy — using scans like SPECT and PET. What's the field?
Nuclear medicine: Medical specialty. Nuclear medicine (nuclear radiology) is a medical specialty involving the application of radioactive substances in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.
Nicknamed the fish hawk, this diurnal bird of prey has a wingspan up to 180 centimeters and hunts almost exclusively fish — which bird?
Osprey: Species of bird. The osprey (Pandion haliaetus), historically known as sea hawk, river hawk, and fish hawk, is a diurnal, fish-eating bird of prey with a cosmopolitan range.
Named from the Latin word for 'sparrow,' this bird order — making up over half of all species — is defined by perching feet with three toes forward and one back. What's it called?
Passerine: Perching birds of the order Passeriformes.
Its Nahuatl name means 'caterpillar cocoon,' but this spineless desert cactus is better known for containing the psychoactive alkaloid mescaline — what is it?
Peyote: Species of psychoactive cactus. Peyote, also known as Lophophora williamsii, is a small, spineless cactus which contains psychoactive alkaloids, particularly mescaline.
This self-limiting skin condition begins with a single “herald patch” before smaller scaly spots erupt days later, usually clearing up on its own within three months — which condition?
Pityriasis rosea: Skin disease. It usually lasts less than three months and goes away without treatment.
Used to disinfect skin before and after surgery, this antiseptic can cause kidney problems and high blood sodium if applied to large wounds, and comes as a liquid, ointment, or powder — what is it?
Povidone-iodine: Antiseptic solution. Povidone-iodine (PVP-I), also known as iodopovidone, is an antiseptic used for skin disinfection before and after surgery.
This term covers the laws, regulations, and government actions that address issues from education to healthcare to transportation — what is it?
Public policy: Government proposals, principles and actions.
Found in the Atlas Mountains as the only member of its family native to Africa, this large ruminant's males are called stags and females are hinds — what species is it?
Red deer: Species of hoofed mammal.

This interdisciplinary field combines a power source, mechanical construction, control circuits, and software to design machines that assist humans in fields from medicine to space exploration — what is it?
Robotics: Design, construction, use, and application of robots.

A member of the mint family native to the Mediterranean, this grayish-leaved perennial subshrub is used both in cooking and as an ornamental garden plant — which herb, better known by its common name sage?
Salvia officinalis: Species of plant. Salvia officinalis, common sage or sage, is a perennial, evergreen subshrub, with woody stems, grayish leaves, and blue to purplish flowers.
Rising from general secretary in 1981 to FIFA's eighth president in 1998, this Swiss administrator won re-election four times before being suspended in the 2015 corruption scandal — who is he?

This informal name applies to any shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc — a body plan that evolved independently many times through convergent evolution across unrelated lineages. What creature is it?
Slug: Shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc. Slug or land slug is a common name for any apparently shell-less terrestrial gastropod mollusc.

Numbering more than 9,000 species, these tiny hexapods are no longer classified as true insects and get their scientific class name from Greek words meaning 'glue' and 'peg,' after a structure called the collophore — what are they called?
Known in antiquity as 'oil of vitriol,' this odorless, syrupy liquid is so thirsty for water that it never occurs pure in nature and will char nearly anything it touches — which substance is it?

Named after the mathematician who introduced it in 1715, this infinite sum built from a function's derivatives at a single point becomes a special case named for Colin Maclaurin when centered at zero — what is it?
Taylor series: Mathematical approximation of a function.
In the standard anatomical position, this is the outermost digit of the hand, right next to the index finger — which digit, known in Latin as the pollex?
Thumb: First digit of the hand. When a person is standing in the medical anatomical position (where the palm is facing to the front), the thumb is the outermost digit.
Known as a noxious weed for its spiky, woody burs that can puncture bare feet and even bicycle tires, this invasive desert-loving plant is native to Eurasia and Africa — name the species?
Tribulus terrestris: Species of flowering plant. Tribulus terrestris is an annual plant in the caltrop family (Zygophyllaceae) widely distributed around the world.
Developed for chemical warfare after research into pesticide toxicity, this oily amber liquid is lethal in just tens of milligrams and is more potent than sarin — what is this compound?
VX (nerve agent): VX is an extremely toxic synthetic chemical compound in the organophosphorus class, specifically, a thiophosphonate.
Neither bee nor ant despite being closely related, yellowjackets and hornets belong to this narrow-waisted insect group that can deliver a painful sting — what is it?
Wasp: Group of insects. Unlike true parasites, the wasp larvae eventually kill their hosts.

Denied European certification after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, this single-aisle airliner made its maiden flight from Irkutsk in 2017 and is built by a UAC subsidiary of Rostec — which aircraft?
Yakovlev MC-21: Twin-engine Russian jet airliner.
What is the chemical symbol for lithium?
The symbol for lithium is Li. Lithium is a chemical element; it has symbol Li and atomic number 3.

In what year was Joe Manganiello born?
Joe Manganiello: Joseph Michael Manganiello ( MANG-gə-NEL-oh; born December 28, 1976) is an American actor.
In what year was Ncuti Gatwa born?
Ncuti Gatwa: Mizero Ncuti Gatwa (English: (N)SHOO-tee GAT-wah; born 15 October 1992) is a Rwandan-Scottish actor.
In what year was Amitabh Bachchan born?
Amitabh Bachchan (né Srivastava; born 11 October 1942) is an Indian actor, playback singer, and producer who primarily works in Hindi cinema.
In what year did James Gandolfini die?
James Gandolfini: James John Gandolfini (Italian: [ɡandolˈfiːni]; September 18, 1961 – June 19, 2013) was an American actor.
In what year was Alien first released?
Alien is a 1979 science fiction horror film directed by Ridley Scott and written by Dan O'Bannon, based on a story by O'Bannon and Ronald Shusett.
In what year was Wonka first released?
Wonka is a 2023 musical fantasy film directed by Paul King, who co-wrote the screenplay with Simon Farnaby.
In what year was Madame Web first released?
